titleEn: Blow Gently, Let the Water Settle!

pages.text: "My basket! I left it here, but it's gone!" Dingding looked around the flat stone on the bank. The bamboo basket had been there that morning, ready for collecting fallen rice ears. Now only dry grass rustled beside the stone.
Mom, who worked several paddies on her own, came up from below. "I borrowed your basket for a moment to carry rice bundles." "You moved it! It's mine!" Dingding stamped their feet and scowled.
"Waaah! I hate you, Mom!" Dingding shouted. Startled, Mom set down the bundle she was holding. But shouting only made Dingding's chest feel tighter.

Grandma, who had farmed rice all her life, came slowly down from the higher paddy. She held Dingding's hand, and they crouched together on the bank. "Your chest suddenly felt hot, didn't it? That's anger."
Grandma leaned toward the water below and blew gently. Round ripples spread out, faded away, and left the water calm again. "Look. If you blow your anger out like this, it can settle, too."

Dingding leaned toward the water and gave a big, gentle blow. Ripples spread in circles, and the hot feeling slowly left their chest. Grandma said in a singsong voice, "Blow Gently, Let the Water Settle!"
Feeling calmer, Dingding shyly approached Mom. "I'm sorry I shouted. I got angry when my basket was gone." Dingding smiled. "Blow Gently, Let the Water Settle!"

Mom picked up the basket beside the rice bundles and put it in Dingding's hands. "Here, it's yours again." Dingding sniffed the rice smell in the basket. "Let's collect rice ears!" Their mouth curved into a wide smile.

Now Dingding knew what to do when angry. "One, stop when anger rises! Two, blow gently! Three, talk when I'm calm!" The next day, when the jug was missing, Dingding blew first and asked, "Mom, have you seen my water jug?"

Mom hugged Dingding. "When you ask instead of shouting, I can help you find it right away." Anger could be calmed with a gentle breath instead of a shout. Dingding swung the basket and called, "Blow Gently, Let the Water Settle!"
